meta.title: Harold Kamgang · COO at Tunora, process engineer
meta.desc: COO at Tunora, process engineer, dual degree MSc in International Business and MBA. 19 months without a workplace accident on a 70-person industrial site, 8% fewer losses in 6 months.
hero.role: COO at Tunora · Process engineer · MSc and MBA in International Business
hero.pitch: I started as an operator on a flour mill floor. I left supervising 70 people on 3x8 shifts, after 19 months without a workplace accident. Now COO at Tunora, I bring the same discipline to a young team.
hero.cv: Download my CV
hero.avail: Based in Barcelona · French and English native · German B1
stat.1.l: with no workplace accident, across 70 people on three shifts
about.p1: Trained as a process engineer, I spent 19 months in continuous production at an ISO 9001:2015 certified industrial flour mill in Cameroon, supervising 70 people across three shifts. That is where I learned that quality and safety are not decreed from an office: they are built on the floor, station by station, with the operators.
about.p2: I then earned a dual degree, an MSc in International Business at EAE Business School in Barcelona and an MBA at the Universitat de Lleida, to speak the language of management as well as that of the shop floor. My thesis, written in a team of three, built the B2B partnership strategy of an electric bike tour operator.
tl.coo.x: I set up how a young team runs (decisions traced, a risk register, a WBS and Gantt plan) and I also handle marketing.
about.p3: Since October 2026, I have been COO at Tunora, which turns one sentence into an animated video. I bring the same discipline to a young team: decisions written down and traced, a risk register, a plan. I also handle marketing. If you work on operations, quality or how a small team runs with discipline, get in touch.
tl.0.x: B2B prospecting for schools and language academies, writing the team's sales manual, and drafting a partnership proposal.
tl.1.x: Master's thesis: a partner-led growth strategy for an electric bike tour operator.
tl.2.x: Safety for 70 people on three shifts, ISO 9001:2015 compliance, HACCP audit, continuous improvement and KPI-driven management.
tl.3b.x: Official title of operator, but I was already doing the production supervision work that got formalised a few months later.
tl.3c.x: Layout drawing for a soybean processing plant (silos, extraction, refining, packaging, wastewater treatment): started in AutoCAD, completed in Microsoft Visio once the site's real dimensions turned out to be unavailable.
tl.3.x: Wrote 10 standard operating procedures and their training materials, trained 70 operators, applied 5S.
tl.4.x: Restored inventory accuracy in a high-volume warehouse by reconciling physical stock against ERP records.
tl.5.x: Engineering thesis: a 0.92 correlation between engine liquid waste volume and lubricant consumption (2019 to 2021), a Pareto analysis identifying the 20% of equipment behind 80% of leaks, and a proposed UV detection system.
proj.lead: Eleven situations where I ran operations with discipline: context, action, result. Every figure is verifiable and I can walk through any of them in an interview.
proj.1.c: 70 people on 3x8 shifts in a flour mill, where mechanical risk and dust never go away.
proj.1.a: Team briefings, weekly floor visits, near misses reported and followed up, PPE checked. Every shift leader is involved rather than policed from above.
proj.1.r: 19 consecutive months with no reported workplace accident, from February 2024 to August 2025.
proj.2.t: HACCP audit passed with no major finding
proj.2.c: A food safety audit to pass within three months.
proj.2.a: A mock audit, critical points identified, traceability upgraded, non-conformities resolved, the action plan followed to closure.
proj.2.r: Audit passed with no major finding, within the three-month deadline.
proj.3.t: 8% less waste and 10% more efficiency in 6 months
proj.3.c: High material losses on the line, with poorly documented causes.
proj.3.a: Interns supervised on root-cause analysis (Ishikawa, 5 Whys), standardised settings, 5S, tracking by indicators.
proj.3.r: 8% less waste and 10% more efficiency over six months.
proj.4.c: A compliance programme to roll out across a site with many departments, each with its own habits.
proj.4.a: Risks scored by criticality and occurrence, more than 30 stakeholders aligned, procedures written and updated.
proj.4.r: 100% audit readiness, and an approach the teams understood rather than endured.
proj.5.c: Weekly and monthly reporting done by hand: slow, and a source of copying errors.
proj.5.a: Automation with advanced Excel and Sage X3 ERP queries, then dashboards for management.
proj.5.r: 40% less reporting time, and decisions made on current data.
proj.6.c: A thesis in a team of three for an electric bike tour operator in Barcelona, dependent on online agencies.
proj.6.a: A weighted selection grid, six field interviews, nine market sources, a standardised document base.
proj.6.r: Twenty priority partners, three incentive models, a 90-day pilot with measurable thresholds, and €38,500 to €75,700 of additional net revenue.
proj.7.t: Kribi: 200 of 250 maintenance interventions caused by oil leaks
proj.7.c: A 216 MW plant whose oily water was neither measured nor linked to its causes.
proj.7.a: Correlations on three years of data, a Pareto of the equipment, an Ishikawa of the treatment unit.
proj.7.r: A 0.92 correlation between liquid waste and oil consumption (2019 to 2021), 20% of the equipment behind 80% of leaks, and ultraviolet detection proposed.
sk.2.c: Risk assessment scored on severity and frequency
sk.5.a: Microsoft Office · advanced Excel (formulas, pivot tables, charts)
soft.lead: A list of adjectives proves nothing. Each quality below is tied to a real situation.
soft.1.p: Training 70 operators on 10 procedures does not happen through a memo. I learned to explain a technical requirement to someone who does not share my vocabulary, and to check it was understood before considering it applied.
soft.2.p: Six years of Toastmasters, including a term as VP Public Relations. That is what lets me run a safety briefing for a night shift, carry an initiative in front of 30-plus stakeholders, and present results to management without drowning them.
soft.3.p: An audit is prepared in three months, or it fails. Risk scoring, action plan, dates, owners: I have got into the habit of working with dated deliverables rather than intentions.
soft.4.p: When material losses rise, intuition is not enough. Ishikawa, 5 Whys, data pulled from the ERP: I trace the cause before proposing an action, and I measure afterwards.
soft.5.p: I have worked in Cameroon and studied in Spain. French and English native, German B1, Spanish A1. I adapt to the person in front of me rather than the other way round.

edu.2.x: Two degrees from a single programme, MBA earned with 16.88/20. Thesis: a partner-led growth strategy for Pink Ducks.

int.2: One book a month, mostly personal development and management.
int.3: Five years in a choir, tenor section, I can read simple sheet music.
int.4: Passionate about languages and classical poetry: four languages, two of them native.

proj.10.t: Wood waste pyrolysis: a project run end to end
proj.10.c: Wood makes up 27% of Cameroon's hazardous waste, with no recovery process studied.
proj.10.a: A paired project with objectives, milestones, a schedule and a 98,000 FCFA budget; a fixed-bed reactor instrumented by ourselves.
proj.10.r: An average heating rate of about 1.3 K/minute (about 420°C reached in 330 minutes) in the fixed-bed reactor, and a two-part reactor designed to capture the gases rather than release them.
proj.11.t: Composting: 30,000 FCFA of margin per tonne
proj.11.c: A coffee roaster threw away chaff and shavings without having measured the volume.
proj.11.a: The stream quantified, a real trial on six containers over thirteen days, an economic case benchmarked against a real competitor.
proj.11.r: 2,794 kg of recoverable waste per year, and 30,000 FCFA of margin per tonne of fertiliser sold.
proj.8.c: An engineering degree that requires a documented fieldwork project every year.
proj.8.a: Dibamba thermal plant, natural pesticide from nkui spices, composting, pyrolysis, Kribi oily water.
proj.8.r: Four of the five projects circle one question: what do you do with what the facility discharges? Degree earned at 15/20, with Distinction.
proj.9.t: Barcelona CycleGuide: a voice app delivered end to end

proj.9.a: Built with an AI assistant: React Native and Firebase, custom geofencing, a multilingual voice assistant. Switched platforms when the first one hit its limit.
proj.9.r: A functional prototype tested on real iPhone and Android devices, delivered with technical documentation and a handover guide for a non-technical founder.

tl.7.x: Unrecovered waste quantified at 2,794 kg a year, a lab composting trial across six samples over thirteen days, and a costed process yielding 30,000 FCFA margin per tonne.
tl.8.r: Practical work: sesame oil and natural pesticide
tl.8.x: Sesame oil production, and assisting on a natural pesticide made from nkui spices, including African pepper.
